judged_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — P1, confidence 75, advisory: works with provider-specific parsing while sharing is disabled, but when sharing is enabled `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` creates a literal object-string key rather than a numeric catch-all and Zod strips the advertised expiry field, so Office 365 retains an expired `expires_in` and recontacts the sync endpoint on every operation; although a custom endpoint can choose its expiry field, no normal field is captured by this schema, so the amplification remains.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts. Looking at lines 7-10, the schema uses `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` which creates a literal string key '[object Object]' rather than a dynamic catch-all for numeric expiry fields. This means when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, the minimumTokenResponseSchema won't properly capture expiry fields like 'expires_in' or 'expiry_date' from OAuth responses. The schema only validates access_token exists but doesn't properly handle expiry fields, which could cause tokens to be treated as expired or not properly tracked.
